WhatI havelearned
Seljuk Dynasty (11th-13th century) founded by nomadic Turkish tribe ruled Persia,
Iraq,SyriaandAnatolia.
Nizam al-Mulk a Persian vizier of Seljuk Dynasty founded and promoted madrassa as
a centre of learning.
Fatimid Dynasty was founded in 909 AD Ubayd Allah al-Mahdi Billah.
Under Fatimid Egypt became the political, cultural, and religious centre of the
empire.

Ayyubid recaptured Jerusalem from the Crusaders in 1187.
Safavid Dynasty was founded by Ismail -1. The dynasty was at its peak during rule of

In 1096 AD, European armies gathered in the Byzantinecapital of Constantinople and
theyplannedtoattackPalestinefromthere.
The city of Jerusalem is considered a holy city equally by thefollowers of three major
religions.
The crusades weremainlyfought to regain the holy land of Jerusalem.
Sultan Salah ud Din Ayyubi was the hero of many battles and faced the Crusaders for
about twenty years.Ultimately, he pushed back thecombinedforces of Europe.
The defeat of the Crusaders diminished the power of Pope and Nobles which
strengthened the power of the Kings.
The Ottoman Empire was founded in 1299 AD after the collapse of the Anatolian
SeljukEmpire.
The Ottoman Caliphate started in 1517 AD, when Sultan SelimIconquered Egyptby
defeatingtheMamluks.

The ClassicalAge of the Ottoman Empirelasted from the Conquest ofConstantinople
in1453until thedeath of Suleyman theMagnificent in1566.
The Ottomans had great influence on the world politics, as theywere considered the
nightmare of the tyrants and the saviour of the oppressed.
Thebasic education in the Ottoman Empire was free of cost for all citizens,and
includedboth classical and contemporary subjects
The Ottoman Empire was officially dissolved on October 29, 1923with the
proclamation of the Republic of Turkey.
